what_it_is: ElecBench is an evaluation framework and test set for LLMs in power-system operation and dispatch (p.1). It defines six primary metrics (factuality, logicality, stability, fairness, security, expressiveness) with 24 sub-metrics, and three scenarios: general, power operations (dispatch, operation monitoring) and fault diagnosis and recovery (black start) (pp.1-3, p.12). Items come from a private set (papers, regulations and textbooks turned into question-answer pairs, plus power-system simulation data), from electrical-engineering items in C-Eval and MMLU, and from GPT-4-generated fictional concepts for the hallucination and source-validity metrics (pp.9-10). Responses are compared with standard answers and scored by two independent GPT-4 judges, with a human deciding when their scores differ beyond a threshold; stability is scored by similarity before and after perturbation (p.11). Eight LLMs were evaluated (p.12).
domain: engineering: electrical, power-system operation and dispatch (p.1)
size: item count not stated in the text; 6 metrics, 24 sub-metrics, 3 scenarios (p.1, p.12); 8 models: GPT-3.5, GPT-4, LLaMA2 7B/13B/70B, GAIA 7B/13B/70B (p.12)
source_of_items: mixed: professional literature and textbooks converted to question-answer pairs, simulation-generated power-system scenarios, electrical-engineering items selected from C-Eval and MMLU, and GPT-4-generated fictional concepts checked by search engine (pp.9-10)
instances: static released test set, partly built from simulation runs and GPT-4 generation (pp.9-10, p.14)
has_gold_traces: no: responses are compared with standard answers (p.11)
evaluation: LLM judge: two independent GPT-4 scorers against standard answers, with human evaluation when they disagree beyond a threshold; similarity scores for stability; manual search-engine checks for information reliability; simulation outputs scored for security and accuracy (p.11). The logicality metric targets 'the logical rigour of the entire reasoning process ... rather than directly on the accuracy of the conclusions' (p.5).
human_validation: Undergraduates with a power-systems background selected content (p.9); professionals resolved disagreements between two GPT-4 scenario classifiers (p.10); humans adjudicate disagreements between the two GPT-4 judges (p.11). No agreement statistics or judge-versus-human accuracy are reported.

engtrace_use.explanation: ElecBench is confined to the power sector, specifically power-system operation and dispatch (p.1, p.12), so the characterization holds. Two citation faults remain: the sentence never names ElecBench, so a reader cannot match the key to any of the three names given for five keys; and the first author of the cited arXiv version is Xiyuan Zhou, with Yuheng Cheng third (p.1), so the key should be 'Zhou et al., 2024'.
